settings.text:
Checking for argon gas in double-glazed glass using an automatic single-outlet gas filling machine is a useful way to monitor the condition and quality of these products.
The type of gas filling the cavity between the panes is an important factor in improving the performance and insulating properties of double-glazed glass.
Understanding argon gas filling in double-glazed glass, and its impact on glass quality and performance, is essential when checking whether argon gas is present in the unit.
This article explains an effective way to check for argon gas in double-glazed glass using an automatic single-outlet gas filling machine.

settings.title: Why It Is Important to Check Argon Gas in Double-Glazed Glass
settings.text:
Checking for argon gas in double-glazed glass is one of several procedures used to assess product performance and quality, alongside investigating issues such as sound transmission through double-glazed windows, how sealant is applied, causes of glass fogging, the performance of double glazing, and gaps between the panes.
A temperature difference can be felt on the two sides of a double-glazed unit. Filling the cavity with argon helps the glass function as a thermal insulator.
If a sufficient amount of argon has been injected between the panes, the outer pane exposed to cold outdoor air should be colder than the inner pane exposed to indoor conditions.
This temperature difference can be easily detected by touch.
To improve the insulation of double-glazed glass and retain argon more effectively, it is important to use continuous spacer bars.
An argon gas valve on the aluminium spacer of a double-glazed unit is an indication that argon may be present inside the glass and can help identify gas-filled units.

settings.title: Methods for Checking Argon Gas in Double-Glazed Glass
settings.text:
Argon presence in double-glazed glass can be checked using several basic methods.
The following are some practical ways to check for argon in double-glazed units:
1. One basic but time-consuming method is to immerse the units in water for several hours and then expose them to sunlight. If condensation appears inside the glass, argon is not present.
2. Another method is to use an argon gas filling machine. The procedure may vary depending on whether it is used with UPVC windows or other double-glazed products. However, certain testing principles should be applied consistently to all double-glazed units. An automatic single-outlet gas filling machine can be used to perform this test and check for argon in the unit.
3. Another basic approach is to look for signs that argon is absent. Double-glazed glass without argon or another filling gas may use ordinary air in the cavity; vacuum insulation is another approach used in some products to reduce sound and heat transfer. Similar gas-free insulated cavities can be found in thermal flasks.

settings.title: An Introduction to Argon Gas Filling Machines for Double-Glazed Glass
settings.text:
An argon gas filling machine for double-glazed glass is a practical and systematic tool for checking the presence of gas in double-glazed units.
Argon gas filling machines have an inlet connected to the gas supply and between one and eight outlets. They are manufactured and supplied in both automatic and manual versions.

1. Automatic Argon Gas Filling Machine

This type of argon gas filling machine is equipped with a PLC. After calculating the volume between the two panes, it determines the amount of argon required for the double-glazed unit. The entered spacer length, width and cavity dimensions enable the machine to calculate the required gas volume accurately. This makes the automatic model highly precise.

2. Manual Argon Gas Filling Machine

This model is generally more economical than the automatic version. After switching on the machine, the operator controls the gas output by setting the injection duration. Its accuracy when checking for argon in double-glazed glass after filling is lower than that of the automatic model.
